**Finding: missing (high severity) — Termination for convenience**

The Agreement has a three-year term (§8.1) with auto-renewing Order Forms (§8.2), but Section 9 contains only cause-based exits — material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and Customer's special triggers for security incidents/SLA misses/legal violations/infringement (9.3). Other exits (6.2 acceptance failure, 19.4 warranty, 20.5 infringement, 27.3 force majeure) are all fault- or event-based. A full-text search confirms no convenience right exists anywhere, and there is no §9.4.

Under the rule, no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory, so this fails the fallback. Notably, Vendor also has no convenience right, which is favourable to us and preserved.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** new §9.4 inserted after p0040 giving Customer a 30-day convenience termination in whole or in part, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no early-termination charge, and express confirmation that Vendor has no convenience right during a term. The comment offers 60 days' notice as a fallback if needed.
